newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall as liquidity dries up.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall as liquidity dries up.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended lower on poor volume on Friday following Thursday's decision by the Constitutional Court that the EU association accord cannot be ratified before the country's legislation is changed.
Traders said the SBI index could fall by three to four percent over the next week.
The SBI index eased 0.51 percent or 6.77 points to 1,309.19. This week the blue-chip index fell a total 1.07 percent.
"The index is most likely to stagnate until the constitution is changed, after that it could rise a little, but just over the short-term," said Andrej Potocnik, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
The Ljubljana bourse on Friday announced that it had changed the SBI index at the beginning of the month to include port operator Luka Koper.
At the same time the bourse excluded pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus and financial consultancy Nika .
Overall seven shares fell, five rose and two were flat, while 14 were untraded. Turnover slumped to 36.3 million tolars from 88.6 million.
"Even turnover of around 100 million tolars is negligible, and I expect it to stay at these levels until foreign players resume their buying," one trader said.

The central bank in February blocked foreign activity, ordering international investors to open custodian accounts at one of Slovenian 14 fully licensed banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenian shares.
Since then the index has dropped by over 20 percent while average daily volumes tumbled by about 80 percent.

Traders see ratification of the EU association treaty, signed in June last year as a pre-condition for international investors to resume buying, which is expected to improve liquidity on the Ljubljana bourse.
Petrol trading firm Petrol had the highest turnover, easing 0.89 percent to 16,760 tolars on volume of 683 shares for total turnover of 11.5 million tolars.

Traders said Petrol will continue to be one of most interesting shares due to its strategic importance and business performance, although it is seen moving between 16,000 and 17,000 tolars over the short-term.
Ordinary shares of Dolenjska bank led the day's decliners, tumbling 5.24 percent to 14,100 tolars on volume of 42 shares on a technical correction.
Luka Koper was the top gainer, soaring 2.51 percent to 1,799 tolars on volume of 1,000 shares on expectations of a dividend payout.

Bank Hmezad, which announced a fall in its 1996 net to 28.8 million tolars from 105.6 million, was untraded today, offered at a selling indication only. The share was last traded on April 14. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
